transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Maya (Zenith CTO), Jonas (Head of ML), Priya (Infra)

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ava from Redwood, AE on this account; with me is Diego, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Maya: Doing well, thanks. Busy week but good to connect.
[00:08] Jonas: Hi all. Ready to dig in, we've been looking at moving some workloads off OpenAI into something more predictable.
[00:13] Diego: Great, quick agenda: understand your constraints (latency, cost, compliance), discuss Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private, and then technical compatibility with vLLM/TGI and eval parity.
[00:22] Priya: Sounds good. From infra side, main concerns are VPC peering, egress control, and keys — we use KMS and need audit logs.
[00:30] Ava: Perfect. Maya, can you give us a bit of background — what are you running today, volumes, models, that sort of thing?
[00:37] Maya: Sure. We're currently on OpenAI's hosted API for chat and some embeddings. Peak is around 200 req/s, average seq lengths around 512 tokens for chat. We also run a couple of internal reranking pipelines with longer context. Monthly spend north of $60k and trending up; we'd like predictability.
[00:55] Jonas: We also have some experiments using an open stack — trying vLLM for internal batch jobs and TGI for experimentation. The concern is parity: when we move to Dedicated we need behavior identical enough that our evals don't regress.
[01:10] Diego: Totally. We do model cataloging and try to maintain behavioral parity but there are always tokenizer quirks and sampling differences. We can run eval parity tests — at least token-level and logprob comparisons — and threshold regressions.
[01:25] Jonas: Ok, important for us. Also curious about latency. Our SLO is 100-150ms p50 on short prompts; OpenAI is hitting that today in most regions.
[01:35] Ava: For Dedicated we can size GPU pools to hit those latencies; Diego can talk about kernel selection and batching.
[01:41] Diego: Right — runtime chooses kernels based on model shape and sequence distribution. Continuous batching helps throughput but we can tune max-latency buckets. For 512 tokens and p50 ~120ms we'll likely use smaller batch windows and prefer tensorized kernels on A100s or equivalent.
[01:58] Jonas: How does KV caching interact if we have lots of chat?
[02:02] Diego: We support prefix/KV caching — big wins for chat. In Dedicated you can configure cache residency and eviction; small note, sometimes transcripts show 'K-V cache' in our logs so the auto-transcription may spell it weird.
[02:14] Maya: (laughs) transcription is always weird. Another big question: will our prompts produce the same output? We have evaluation suites with specific pass rates.
[02:23] Diego: We usually run end-to-end evals: tokenization alignment, sampling RNG seed consistency where possible, and metric level checks. For some models there are small PRNG differences; we log and flag them. We can also pin model versions.
[02:36] Priya: For network, can Dedicated be in our VPC? We need private connectivity and no public egress for some PHI workloads.
[02:43] Ava: We offer Private deployments with customer VPC and into-your-account options. For Dedicated we have a dedicated tenant model — if you need full private control we can talk about our Private/VPC deployment which includes KMS integrations and audit logs.
[02:58] Priya: Good. And SSO — SAML and RBAC?
[03:02] Diego: Yes, SAML/SSO, SCIM, RBAC at route/model level. Audit trails are retained — retention configurable as an add-on.
[03:10] Jonas: Let's talk migration effort. We have about 20 production endpoints right now. How heavy is the SDK change?
[03:17] Ava: Minimal — we support OpenAI-compatible API surface for most calls (chat, completion, embeddings). There are some differences for advanced params but the SDKs make it straightforward.
[03:28] Maya: Pricing model? We need predictable unit cost.
[03:31] Ava: Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated has reserved capacity pricing with monthly commits. There's also per-token accounting and optional egress fees for Private deployments. I'll send a pricing spreadsheet after the call.
[03:43] Jonas: On the technical compatibility note — with vLLM/TGI experiments, we saw differences in memory usage and batching behavior. Can you run a benchmark against our vLLM configs?
[03:52] Diego: Yes, we'll set up a parity benchmark. For vLLM/TGI we often replicate the same model weights and run shared prompts. Two caveats: quantization differences can change outputs and latencies — we can test FP16 and int8 profiles.
[04:06] Priya: Do you support host-based HSM or customer-managed keys?
[04:10] Diego: We integrate with cloud KMS and HSM options via standard APIs, and for Private we can support customer-managed keys.
[04:16] Maya: Any compliance certifications? We need SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 for procurement.
[04:22] Ava: We are SOC2 and have ISO docs; I'll share the whitepaper and SOC2 report under NDA.
[04:28] Maya: Great. What about model updates/rollout? We don't want sudden regressions in prod.
[04:33] Diego: Rollouts can be canaryed, A/Bed, and we have automatic fallback policies to older pinned model versions. Also Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization and model variants based on workload.
[04:45] Jonas: About storage and logs — do you retain any request/response data by default? We currently redact PHI before sending to OpenAI.
[04:53] Ava: For Hosted we have configurable retention; for Dedicated/Private there are policies and can be disabled. We recommend token-level cost/latency analytics with redaction options.
[05:02] Maya: Ok. Can you walk through a sample benchmark plan?
[05:06] Diego: Sure — phase 1: tokenization and deterministic output comparison on a fixed eval set (1k prompts). Phase 2: latency/throughput tests under realistic arrival patterns using your seq length distribution. Phase 3: long-context/kv cache tests and reranker throughput. We'll collect p50/p90/p99 and cost-per-1k tokens.
[05:29] Jonas: Timeline? We'd like a POC in 3-4 weeks if the numbers look good.
[05:34] Ava: That's reasonable. We'll kick off with a benchmark run and a Dedicated sizing recommendation.
[05:39] Priya: From procurement perspective, what SLA do you offer for Dedicated?
[05:43] Ava: We have SLA tiers for Dedicated with SLO targets; for enterprise commitments we include uptime and latency targets. I'll include the SLA doc with pricing.
[05:50] Maya: Any risks or gotchas we should watch for?
[05:53] Diego: Biggest surprises are usually tokenization mismatches and quantization-induced quality changes. Also, network egress and cold-start latencies for certain GPU configs. We'll try to surface those in the benchmark.
[06:08] Jonas: For eval parity, we need raw logprobs — is that available?
[06:12] Diego: Yes, logprobs and token-level outputs are available. For private setups we can make sure only authorized roles can access them.
[06:19] Maya: Sounds good. Any competitor comparison we should know?
[06:22] Ava: Customers often compare us to OpenAI for hosted simplicity, Anthropic for certain model families, and pure self-hosting with vLLM/TGI for cost. Our stance is we provide unified runtime and the operational lift so you don't manage every host.
[06:36] Jonas: Okay, last thing — can we do a quick recap of next steps?
[06:40] Ava: Sure. Diego will prepare the benchmark plan and capacity config. I'll send pricing, SOC2/ISO, and SLA docs. Priya will share infra/network diagram and any outbound policy. We aim to kick the POC next week.
[06:53] Priya: I'll share the diagram today.
[06:55] Ava: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the benchmark template.
[06:59] Maya: Thanks, bye.
[07:01] (meeting ends)

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., 'v vLM' or 'Antropic' instead of Anthropic). References: pricing spreadsheet link (sent post-call), SOC2 whitepaper (link to be shared under NDA), benchmark template (drive link).

Transcript end.
